sections.title: The Hook: Dynamics in Motion
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'change' as a function of time. Use a visual of a rabbit population growing or a drone accelerating. Explain that while algebraic equations solve for a fixed point, ODEs describe the trajectory of a state over time.
sections.example: A drone pilot wants to know its position at any second based on its current velocity (acceleration rate).

sections.title: Defining the ODE: The Language of Change
sections.content: Define an ODE as an equation involving a function and its derivatives. Use a split-screen animation: left side shows the physical change (moving object), right side shows the mathematical notation: dy/dx = f(x, y).
sections.example: Representing Newton's Law of Cooling as dT/dt = -k(T - T_env).

sections.title: Visualization: The Direction Field
sections.content: Explain that solving an ODE is like finding a path through a field of arrows (vectors). Show an animation where thousands of tiny arrows represent the slope of the function at every point, and a 'solution curve' traces a path through them.
sections.example: Visualize the 'slope field' of dy/dx = y; the curves show exponential growth emanating from different starting points.

sections.title: Initial Conditions: Pinning Down the Solution
sections.content: Explain that an ODE describes a family of curves. We need an 'Initial Condition' (the starting state) to select the specific curve that matches our real-world scenario.
sections.example: If a rocket is launched, the ODE tells us its potential paths, but the 'Initial Condition' (launch height = 0) tells us exactly which path the rocket will take.

sections.title: Conclusion & Summary
sections.content: Summarize the cycle: Model the change (ODE) -> Visualize the field -> Apply Initial Conditions -> Find the specific path. Emphasize that ODEs turn 'laws of nature' into 'predictive tools'.
sections.example: From predicting the spread of a virus to the path of a planet, ODEs are the universal map for dynamic systems.
